title: Coin Change II
keyIdea: Count combinations (order doesn't matter) with unlimited coins. dp[a] = ways to make a. Loop coins outside, amounts inside: dp[a] += dp[a − coin]. That counts each multiset once.

approaches.name: One-row DP (coins outside)
approaches.idea: I wrote this one (you didn't paste code). dp[0] = 1; for each coin, for a = coin..amount: dp[a] += dp[a − coin]. Unsigned so middle values may wrap safely.
approaches.why: Two loops; one row of amount + 1 counts.

quiz.q: Why loop over coins on the outside?
options: Each combination is then built in one fixed coin order, so it is counted once

quiz.q: What does looping amounts on the outside count instead?
options: Ordered sequences (permutations), as in LC 377 Combination Sum IV

quiz.q: Why go a upward (not downward) here?
options: Coins are unlimited, so dp[a − coin] may already use this coin
